answer.answer:
The court is a rectangle marked out with lines 40 mm wide (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 1.1).
A shuttle landing on a line is 'in': all the lines form part of the area which they define (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 1.3), and it is a fault only if the shuttle lands outside the boundaries of the court, i.e. not on or within the boundary lines (Clause 13.3.1). The Line Judge therefore makes no 'Out' call; if the shuttle lands in, the Line Judge says nothing but points to the line with the right hand while looking towards the Umpire (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 8.4).
For contrast with the on-the-line case: if the shuttle lands out, the Line Judge calls 'Out' promptly with both arms extended horizontally (ITTO 7.0 (5), Clause 8.3), but must not call or signal until the shuttle has touched the floor or anything outside the court boundaries, except a player (Clause 8.6); a line judge indicates whether a shuttle landed 'in' or 'out' on the line(s) assigned (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), Clause 17.4).
